roc_auc_below_0.5_root_cause.contrast_with_hi_small: HI-Small achieved 0.8986 to 0.9555 ROC-AUC across all models.
roc_auc_below_0.5_root_cause.scientific_explanation: The ROC-AUC depression in Combined (0.44-0.46) and LI-Medium subset (0.45-0.54) is strictly driven by extreme class imbalance. Combined training data has only 15 positive laundering transactions out of 300,000 samples (0.005% positive rate), which divides into only 5 positive samples per client across 3 federated clients. Similarly, LI-Medium subset training data has only 9 positive transactions out of 200,000 samples (0.0045% positive rate, or 3 positives per client). With so few positive examples per client, the recurrent networks cannot learn discriminative temporal sequences and produce near-constant low scores, leading to random-walk ROC-AUC near 0.50. In sharp contrast, HI-Small has 2,299 positive transactions in training (~766 per client), enabling all 12 models to reliably learn discriminative features and achieve ROC-AUC between 0.8986 and 0.9555. Importantly, labels are NOT inverted, scores are properly oriented (higher score = laundering), and metrics are computed on continuous probability scores.

threshold_selection_integrity.description: Validation threshold tau was frozen based on validation PR-AUC / alert budget and applied directly to test predictions without peeking.

algorithm_comparison_summary.observation: FedAvg consistently outperforms FedProx (mu=0.0001) across all architectures and partitions on HI-Small.
